articles.title: Global Market: China's yuan hits more than four-year high against dollar
articles.content: In a remarkable turn of events, China's yuan has surged against the US dollar, hitting levels unseen in over four years. This strength is linked to a declining dollar and prevailing central bank strategies. Although the People's Bank of China set a midpoint lower than anticipated, its actions aim to moderate currency appreciation. Analysts believe the yuan's resilience may hinge on sustained export performance and domestic demand influences.

articles.title: Indian bonds steady after RBI minutes signal more rate hikes
articles.content: Indian bond yields remain steady at approximately 7.45%, influenced by growing inflation anxieties. The Reserve Bank of India recently increased the repo rate to 5.50%, hinting that further hikes may follow. With climbing oil prices and food inflation heightening economic concerns, analysts speculate another increase may occur in December, before a potential pause. The elevated energy costs pose significant challenges for India's economy, affecting the rupee and government finances.

articles.title: Global Market: Bank of Korea holds interest rates at 3% after back-to-back hikes
articles.content: The Bank of Korea kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.00% on Thursday, pausing after back-to-back 25-basis-point hikes in July and August. The decision was in line with expectations of all 34 economists surveyed by Reuters.
